title: Prefill-decoupled kernel routing and fragment reuse protocol
creator: Diego Ramirez
description: Goal: introduce a prefill-decoupled routing layer that separates kernel selection decisions used for prefill (warmup, KV population) from decode-time kernel routes to reduce p99 stalls and improve reuse of fragmented KV pages. Background: paged attention on long-context models shows recurring stalls when the decode path attempts to rehydrate fragmented KV slots and is forced to migrate or compact synchronously. This ticket implements a lightweight admission + scoring protocol that: (1) proactively schedules micro-prefill work on opportunistic cycles for spans predicted to be hot; (2) exposes a kernel_score vector used at admission to pick a prefill-target kernel that favors zero-copy overlay and fragment co-placement; (3) implements a fragment-reuse policy that assigns soft-residency credits and a speculative restore window to avoid synchronous reclaim during decode spikes.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end tests verifying prefill admission does not increase median decode latency > 2% for short contexts (<512)
p99 decode latency reduced by >= 12% on 32k-context benchmark compared to current mainline when under 80% KV residency pressure
Regression suite showing no increase in token-generation variance for popular models (Llama2-13B, Falcon-40B), with attached perf traces
Automated integration test covering zero-copy overlay path and fallback to copy-based restore with deterministic eviction reproducibility
Design doc and PR reviewed by Runtime and Memory teams, and runbook added to console KB for ops
benchmarks: Preliminary: 32k-context synthetic replay — p99 decode reduced 18% at 75% KV occupancy, throughput +6% on heavy overlap workloads
Microprefill cost delta: average extra GPU cycles for opportunistic micro-prefill = 0.9% under steady load (configurable throttle)
notes: Trade-offs: aggressive micro-prefill improves p99 but increases background GPU utilization; we bias toward tenant-priority and model-affinity to minimize cross-tenant noise.
Design decision: use a small kernel_score vector (residency_score, stride_penalty, quant_compatibility, overlay_friendly) to keep scoring cheap in hot path.
Fallback: if overlay-compatible kernel not available, route prefill to hedged copy-based kernel and mark fragment for deferred coalescing during low-load windows.
Open question: how to surface prefill admission diagnostics in Console without leaking tenant data — plan: expose aggregated counters and sampled per-tenant traces (no token content).
